fact: Owl Press reports mobile money operators Afrimoney and Orange Money among stakeholders at the Flot launch, and says mobile money adoption continues to grow in Sierra Leone.
Afrimoney and Orange Money operate mobile money in Sierra Leone, and central bank data show 8.2 million mobile money accounts at 31 December 2023.

fact: The Sierra Leone Ministry of Communication, Technology and Innovation says mobile money occupies a growing place in the country's financial transactions, including on Orange's network.
Orange Sierra Leone said Orange Money lets customers send and receive money, pay bills, and shop online and in stores.
The Minister told Parliament that Orange Sierra Leone recorded about 390 mobile money fraud complaints in 2026 and operators can freeze mobile money wallets.
The Minister said the government has increased financial inclusion through mobile money services, and that Orange Sierra Leone recorded about 390 mobile money fraud complaints in 2026.

Sierra Leone's Parliament was told of fraud on mobile-money services, mainly on the Orange network, including fraudulent mobile-money requests and unclaimed mobile-money balances, so mobile money is in service (Sierra Leone Monitor, reporting the 4 August 2026 sitting).
The Fintech Times analysis says mobile money operators including Orange Money and Afrimoney let consumers transfer funds, pay bills and purchase goods in Sierra Leone.
NaCSA says grants were paid to beneficiaries in Falaba District through Afri-money, a mobile money service.
Africell Sierra Leone launched the Afrimoney Prepaid Visa Card for Afrimoney mobile money wallets, with Ecobank and Visa, enabling domestic and international digital transactions.
TechAfrica News reports Orange launched the Orange Money Mastercard in Sierra Leone, a virtual card linked to Orange Money wallets.
Orange Money's CEO says the mobile money service has operated since 2016/2017, formerly as Airtel Money, and it signed an agreement with IOM on 14 August 2024 to pay migrants through it.
Orange Money SL and other mobile money providers operate in Sierra Leone, and the workshop sought to secure mobile money services there.

TechAfrica News said Velmie and Metro Cable launched Vult, a digital wallet to send and receive money, pay bills and top up from mobile money, with 475,000+ users in its first year per a later case study.

The Bank of Sierra Leone says its Instant Payment System has operated for under a year with seven banks and two mobile money operators, credited to Orange Money and GTBank for early growth, with about 1.4 million registered users.
The Bank of Sierra Leone says its Instant Payment System enables real-time transfers between banks and mobile money platforms, with about 600,000 transactions by late 2025.
The Bank of Sierra Leone's national Instant Payment System connects banks and mobile money operators in service, while the Salon Payment Switch covers all commercial banks' ATMs.
Africell describes Afrimoney as a mobile money service operating in Sierra Leone, whose wallets customers use to send money, including by USSD.
This Day reports that Afrimoney, a mobile money wallet service, has users in Sierra Leone who can now send money abroad by USSD from 23 May 2025.
